data.gender_notes: Kalidas is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Kali (dark) + das (servant) – A beautiful, skilled poet, often associated with Lord Shiva. The name Kalidas carries the meaning “Beautiful, Skilled Poet” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kalidas usually hope their child will grow to embody beautiful, skilled poet and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Kalidas is widely regarded as one of the greatest Sanskrit poets and playwrights in world literature. His works have had a profound influence on Indian and world literature and continue to captivate audiences with their beauty, depth, and complexity. Some of his most famous works include "Meghaduta," "Ritu Samara," and the plays "Sakuntala" and "Abhijanana Shakuntalam."
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kalidas means "servant of Kali," the Hindu goddess of time, change, and creativity. The name reflects the poet's deep connection to the divine and his role as a vessel for expressing the creative power of the universe. In Hinduism, poetry and literature are considered sacred forms of expression that can connect the individual to the divine. By embracing the name Kalidas, the poet was acknowledging his role as a servant and channel for the divine creative force.
